Acute Heat Stress: Control and A–D at the Same Level

STAT 628 — Part 1 model-building notes

Group project

Fall 2026

1. Data cleaning

The acute experiment has one row per plot. Each treated plot is paired with a nearby control plot that has the same year, cultivar, intensity group, and plot number. The pair is year × cultivar × intensity_group × plot; plot is a block number (1–3) within a cell, not a unique physical plot ID.

The key change here is that Control and A, B, C, D are five levels of one factor, heat_group, rather than a binary treatment plus a separate intensity_group factor. This is the same “common control” parameterisation as the earlier analysis: every heat level is compared with the same control mean, and the model estimates one mean for each of the five levels.

All 48 control plots are untreated (no heat lamps), so they are pooled into a single Control level. The four intensity groups’ control plots are not four different treatments; they all contribute to the same control mean. The four heat levels A–D are compared with that pooled control.

d_raw <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wwy200311gy-sudo/stat628/refs/heads/main/acute_yield_data_fall_2026.csv")

d <- d_raw %>%
  mutate(
    year              = factor(year),
    cultivar          = factor(toupper(trimws(cultivar))),
    intensity_group   = factor(toupper(trimws(intensity_group)),
                               levels = c("D", "C", "B", "A")),
    treatment         = factor(toupper(trimws(treatment)),
                               levels = c("CONTROL", "OTC"),
                               labels = c("Control", "OTC")),
    heat_group        = factor(
      ifelse(treatment == "Control", "Control", as.character(intensity_group)),
      levels = c("Control", "D", "C", "B", "A")
    ),
    pair              = interaction(year, cultivar, intensity_group, plot,
                                    drop = TRUE),
    total_weight      = healthy_weight + rotten_weight,
    healthy_count_pct = 100 * healthy_n / (healthy_n + rotten_n),
    healthy_weight_prop = healthy_weight / total_weight,
    healthy_weight_pct  = 100 * healthy_weight_prop,
    pulses            = as.numeric(c(A = 4, B = 3, C = 2, D = 1)[
                                      as.character(intensity_group)])
  )

# Design checks -------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 96, nlevels(d$pair) == 48)
stopifnot(!anyNA(d$heat_group))
stopifnot(all(d %>% count(pair) %>% pull(n) == 2))
stopifnot(all(d %>%
  group_by(pair) %>%
  summarise(ok = setequal(as.character(treatment), c("Control", "OTC")),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(ok)))
stopifnot(all(d$total_weight > 0), all(d$healthy_n + d$rotten_n > 0))

table(d$heat_group, d$treatment) %>%
  kable(caption = "Heat groups: Control is a single level; A–D are the four pulse frequencies.")
Heat groups: Control is a single level; A–D are the four pulse frequencies.
Control OTC
Control 48 0
D 0 12
C 0 12
B 0 12
A 0 12

The design is balanced: 48 control plots and 12 plots for each of A–D, i.e. 3 pairs in every year × cultivar × intensity cell. Control plots received the same insulated OTC without heat lamps, so heat_group = Control is the common reference for all four heat levels.

2. Exploratory analysis

d_long <- d %>%
  select(year, cultivar, heat_group,
         total_weight, healthy_weight, healthy_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_weight, healthy_weight, healthy_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct),
    names_to = "response", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(response = factor(
    response,
    levels = c("total_weight", "healthy_weight", "healthy_count_pct", "healthy_weight_pct"),
    labels = c("Total weight (g)", "Healthy weight (g)",
               "Healthy by count (%)", "Healthy by weight (%)")
  ))

ggplot(d_long, aes(x = heat_group, y = value, fill = cultivar)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7,
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = cultivar),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1,
                                             dodge.width = 0.8),
             alpha = 0.3, size = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(response ~ year, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(MQ = "darkorange", ST = "steelblue")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(MQ = "darkorange", ST = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Heat group (D = 1, C = 2, B = 3, A = 4 pulses)",
       y = NULL, title = "Raw yield responses by heat group, year, and cultivar") +
  theme_report()

Figure 1. Raw distributions of the four yield outcomes by heat group, year, and cultivar. Rows are responses, columns are years, and colours are cultivars; nothing is averaged over year or cultivar. 

d_diff <- d %>%
  select(pair, year, cultivar, intensity_group, treatment,
         total_weight, healthy_weight, healthy_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_weight, healthy_weight, healthy_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct),
    names_to = "response", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(
    diff = OTC - Control,
    response = factor(
      response,
      levels = c("total_weight", "healthy_weight", "healthy_count_pct", "healthy_weight_pct"),
      labels = c("Total weight (g)", "Healthy weight (g)",
                 "Healthy by count (pp)", "Healthy by weight (pp)")
    )
  )

ggplot(d_diff, aes(x = intensity_group, y = diff, colour = cultivar)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey35") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1,
                                             dodge.width = 0.3),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point",
               position = position_dodge(0.3), size = 2.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = cultivar),
               position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  facet_grid(response ~ year, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(MQ = "darkorange", ST = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Intensity group (D = 1, C = 2, B = 3, A = 4 pulses)",
       y = "Heat level minus Control",
       title = "Paired differences by intensity, year, and cultivar") +
  theme_report()

Figure 2. Within-pair differences (heat level minus its paired Control) by intensity, year, and cultivar. Each point is a plot pair; the coloured points and lines are cultivar-specific means.

The weight entries above are raw arithmetic means. The model-based weight means in the next sections are geometric means and are lower (e.g. 808 g for Control total weight); the ratio and percentage-change estimates are unaffected by this distinction.

Figure 1 puts Control and A–D on the same x-axis and separates years (columns) and cultivars (colours); Figure 2 does the same for the paired differences, so the cultivar and year patterns are visible rather than averaged away. The weight differences become more negative with more pulses, while the percentage differences are already large at one pulse. The models below test whether these patterns are consistent across cultivars and years.

3. Model families and candidate structure

Response Family Why
Total weight log-normal LMM positive, right-skewed; variance grows with the mean
Healthy weight log-normal LMM same
Healthy % by count beta-binomial GLMM (logit) counts with extra-binomial variation
Healthy % by weight beta GLMM (logit) continuous proportion in (0, 1)

The LMMs are fitted with lme4::lmer; the GLMMs with glmmTMB. All models have a pair random intercept (1 | pair). heat_group varies within a pair (Control vs the paired heat level), so the heat effects are within-pair contrasts; cultivar and year vary between pairs.

The candidate fixed-effect structures are:

Model Mean structure Purpose
H0 heat_group + cultivar + year + year:cultivar additive 5-level model (common control)
H1 heat_group * cultivar + year + year:cultivar does the heat profile differ by cultivar?
H2 heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar does the heat profile differ by year?
H3 heat_group * (cultivar + year) + year:cultivar both
H4 treatment * intensity_group + cultivar + year + year:cultivar design check only: separate control means (not a candidate)

H0 has 5 group means (Control, A, B, C, D). All control plots are untreated and pooled into one Control level, so the model estimates a single control mean. H4 is not a candidate model: it is a design check with separate control means (8 cell means). H0 is H4 with the three constraints Control_A = Control_B = Control_C = Control_D, so the H0-vs-H4 test has 3 df and checks whether the design-based pooling is supported by the data.

4. Model comparison

fit_lmm <- function(form) lmer(form, data = d, REML = FALSE)
fit_bb <- function(form) glmmTMB(form, data = d, family = betabinomial(),
                                 dispformula = ~ treatment)
fit_beta <- function(form) glmmTMB(form, data = d, family = beta_family(),
                                  dispformula = ~ treatment)

# Total weight
h0_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h1_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * cultivar + year +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h2_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h3_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * (cultivar + year) +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h4_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ treatment * intensity_group +
                      cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair))

# Healthy weight
h0_healthy <- fit_lmm(log(healthy_weight) ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                        year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h1_healthy <- fit_lmm(log(healthy_weight) ~ heat_group * cultivar + year +
                        year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h2_healthy <- fit_lmm(log(healthy_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                        year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h3_healthy <- fit_lmm(log(healthy_weight) ~ heat_group * (cultivar + year) +
                        year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h4_healthy <- fit_lmm(log(healthy_weight) ~ treatment * intensity_group +
                        cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair))

# Count percentage
h0_count <- fit_bb(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                     year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h1_count <- fit_bb(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group * cultivar + year +
                     year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h2_count <- fit_bb(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                     year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h3_count <- fit_bb(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group * (cultivar + year) +
                     year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h4_count <- fit_bb(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ treatment * intensity_group +
                     cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair))

# Weight percentage
h0_wpct <- fit_beta(healthy_weight_prop ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h1_wpct <- fit_beta(healthy_weight_prop ~ heat_group * cultivar + year +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h2_wpct <- fit_beta(healthy_weight_prop ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h3_wpct <- fit_beta(healthy_weight_prop ~ heat_group * (cultivar + year) +
                      year:cultivar + (1 | pair))
h4_wpct <- fit_beta(healthy_weight_prop ~ treatment * intensity_group +
                      cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair))

aic_tab <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(Response = "Total",   Model = c("H0", "H1", "H2", "H3"),
             df = sapply(list(h0_total, h1_total, h2_total, h3_total),
                         function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
             AIC = sapply(list(h0_total, h1_total, h2_total, h3_total), AIC)),
  data.frame(Response = "Healthy", Model = c("H0", "H1", "H2", "H3"),
             df = sapply(list(h0_healthy, h1_healthy, h2_healthy, h3_healthy),
                         function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
             AIC = sapply(list(h0_healthy, h1_healthy, h2_healthy, h3_healthy), AIC)),
  data.frame(Response = "Count",   Model = c("H0", "H1", "H2", "H3"),
             df = sapply(list(h0_count, h1_count, h2_count, h3_count),
                         function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
             AIC = sapply(list(h0_count, h1_count, h2_count, h3_count), AIC)),
  data.frame(Response = "Weight",  Model = c("H0", "H1", "H2", "H3"),
             df = sapply(list(h0_wpct, h1_wpct, h2_wpct, h3_wpct),
                         function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
             AIC = sapply(list(h0_wpct, h1_wpct, h2_wpct, h3_wpct), AIC))
) %>%
  group_by(Response) %>%
  mutate(dAIC = AIC - min(AIC)) %>%
  ungroup()

lrt_row <- function(m_small, m_big, label) {
  a <- anova(m_small, m_big)
  df_col <- if ("Chi Df" %in% names(a)) a[["Chi Df"]] else a[["Df"]]
  data.frame(Test = label, Chisq = a$Chisq[2], df = df_col[2],
             p = a$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])
}

bind_rows(
  lrt_row(h0_total,   h1_total,   "Total: heat × cultivar"),
  lrt_row(h0_total,   h2_total,   "Total: heat × year"),
  lrt_row(h0_total,   h3_total,   "Total: heat × (cultivar + year)"),
  lrt_row(h0_healthy, h1_healthy, "Healthy: heat × cultivar"),
  lrt_row(h0_healthy, h2_healthy, "Healthy: heat × year"),
  lrt_row(h0_healthy, h3_healthy, "Healthy: heat × (cultivar + year)"),
  lrt_row(h0_count,   h1_count,   "Count: heat × cultivar"),
  lrt_row(h0_count,   h2_count,   "Count: heat × year"),
  lrt_row(h0_count,   h3_count,   "Count: heat × (cultivar + year)"),
  lrt_row(h0_wpct,    h1_wpct,    "Weight: heat × cultivar"),
  lrt_row(h0_wpct,    h2_wpct,    "Weight: heat × year"),
  lrt_row(h0_wpct,    h3_wpct,    "Weight: heat × (cultivar + year)")
) %>%
  mutate(p = fmt_p(p)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Likelihood-ratio tests for the 5-level heat_group candidate models.")

What the comparison says.

  • Total and healthy weight: heat_group × year is strongly supported (p = 0.0003 and p = 0.006), while heat_group × cultivar is not (p = 0.28 and p = 0.29). The pooled-control model is used by design; the separate-control check is not significant (p = 0.79 and p = 0.88). The selected weight model is H2: heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar. The heat profile differs between 2024 and 2025, but not between MQ and ST.
  • Count percentage: no heat interaction is supported (heat × cultivar p = 0.95, heat × year p = 0.34, both p = 0.74). The pooled-control model is used by design; the separate-control check is not significant (p = 0.12). The selected model is additive, H0.
  • Weight percentage: no heat interaction is supported (heat × cultivar p = 0.44, heat × year p = 0.82, both p = 0.69). The pooled-control model is used by design; the separate-control check is borderline but not significant (p = 0.10). The selected model is additive, H0. H4 uses three extra parameters for the separate control means; with p = 0.10 for the pooling check, H0 is preferred for parsimony.

For the percentage outcomes, year:cultivar is also not supported (count p = 0.69, weight p = 0.67), so the final additive model drops it:

f_count <- glmmTMB(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                     (1 | pair),
                   data = d, family = betabinomial(),
                   dispformula = ~ treatment)
f_wpct <- glmmTMB(healthy_weight_prop ~ heat_group + cultivar + year +
                    (1 | pair),
                  data = d, family = beta_family(),
                  dispformula = ~ treatment)

aic_pct <- AIC(h0_count, f_count, h0_wpct, f_wpct)
kable(data.frame(Model = rownames(aic_pct), aic_pct, row.names = NULL),
      digits = 2,
      caption = "AIC for the additive percentage models with and without year:cultivar.")

5. Final models

The final models are:

# weights: heat profile varies by year, not by cultivar
log(weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar + (1 | pair)

# percentages: additive 5-level heat effect
count_pct  ~ heat_group + cultivar + year + (1 | pair)   # beta-binomial
weight_pct ~ heat_group + cultivar + year + (1 | pair)   # beta
f_total <- lmer(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                  year:cultivar + (1 | pair),
                data = d, REML = TRUE)
f_healthy <- lmer(log(healthy_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                    year:cultivar + (1 | pair),
                  data = d, REML = TRUE)

tidy_lmm <- function(m) {
  s <- summary(m)$coefficients
  data.frame(Term = rownames(s), Estimate = s[, 1], SE = s[, 2], t = s[, 3],
             row.names = NULL)
}
tidy_glmm <- function(m) {
  s <- summary(m)$coefficients$cond
  data.frame(Term = rownames(s), Estimate = s[, 1], SE = s[, 2],
             z = s[, 3], p = s[, 4], row.names = NULL)
}

5.1 Overall heat effect and A–D versus Control

The average heat effect is the average of the four heat levels minus the common Control: the contrast (-1, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4) over Control, D, C, B, A. This is the natural “heat vs no heat” summary when Control and A–D are at the same level. The A–D versus Control contrasts show which pulse frequencies differ from Control; Holm adjustment is applied within the four contrasts.

avg_heat <- function(fit, by = NULL, type = c("weight", "prop")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  if (is.null(by)) {
    em <- emmeans(fit, ~ heat_group)
  } else {
    em <- emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ heat_group |", by)))
  }
  if (type == "weight") {
    contrast(em, list("Heat avg vs Control" = c(-1, .25, .25, .25, .25)),
             type = "response")
  } else {
    contrast(regrid(em, "response"),
             list("Heat avg vs Control" = c(-1, .25, .25, .25, .25)))
  }
}

ad_heat <- function(fit, by = NULL, type = c("weight", "prop")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  if (is.null(by)) {
    em <- emmeans(fit, ~ heat_group)
  } else {
    em <- emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ heat_group |", by)))
  }
  if (type == "weight") {
    contrast(em, "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "Control", type = "response",
             adjust = "holm")
  } else {
    contrast(regrid(em, "response"), "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "Control",
             adjust = "holm")
  }
}

linear_heat <- function(fit, by = NULL) {
  if (is.null(by)) {
    em <- emmeans(fit, ~ heat_group)
  } else {
    em <- emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ heat_group |", by)))
  }
  # per-pulse linear contrast among D, C, B, A; Control has weight 0
  contrast(em, list("Per-pulse trend" = c(0, -0.3, -0.1, 0.1, 0.3)),
           type = "response")
}

Reading the weight results. The average heat effect is a ratio of about 0.885 for total weight (−11.5%) and 0.804 for healthy weight (−19.6%). But the heat profile is not the same in the two years: in 2024 the average effect is about −8% (total) and −17% (healthy), while in 2025 it is about −15% and −22%. The A–D contrasts show that the 4-pulse treatment (A) is the most damaging in both years, but the dose–response is much steeper in 2025: the per-pulse trend is about −3% in 2024 (not significant) and about −15% in 2025 for total weight. This is the heat_group × year interaction.

Reading the percentage results. The average heat effect is about −12.3 percentage points for count (OR about 0.24) and −8.3 points for weight (OR about 0.19). The four heat levels are all similar: for count, D–A are about −11 to −13 points; for weight, D is the worst (−10 points) and A the least bad (−6 points), but the per-pulse trend is not significant (p ≈ 0.10–0.50). The percentage effect is a step change: any heat pulse lowers the healthy percentage, and additional pulses do not change it much.

Figure 3. Fitted mean total and healthy weight by heat group, year, and cultivar (95% CI). The model has no heat × cultivar interaction, so the MQ and ST curves are parallel; the vertical offset is the cultivar baseline difference. 

prop_emm <- function(m, response) {
  s <- as.data.frame(summary(regrid(emmeans(m, ~ heat_group | year + cultivar), "response")))
  est_name <- setdiff(names(s), c("heat_group", "year", "cultivar", "SE", "df",
                                  "asymp.LCL", "asymp.UCL",
                                  "lower.CL", "upper.CL"))[1]
  data.frame(year = s$year, cultivar = s$cultivar, heat_group = s$heat_group,
             response = response, emmean = s[[est_name]],
             lower = s$asymp.LCL, upper = s$asymp.UCL,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
emm_prop <- bind_rows(
  prop_emm(f_count, "Healthy by count (%)"),
  prop_emm(f_wpct,  "Healthy by weight (%)")
) %>%
  mutate(response = factor(response,
                           levels = c("Healthy by count (%)", "Healthy by weight (%)")))

ggplot(emm_prop, aes(x = heat_group, y = emmean, colour = cultivar, group = cultivar)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.12) +
  facet_grid(response ~ year, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(MQ = "darkorange", ST = "steelblue")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) 100 * x) +
  labs(x = "Heat group (D = 1, C = 2, B = 3, A = 4 pulses)",
       y = "Fitted healthy percentage (%)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Fitted percentages by heat group, year, and cultivar") +
  theme_report()

Figure 4. Fitted healthy percentages by heat group, year, and cultivar (95% CI). The additive model has no heat × year or heat × cultivar interaction, so the curves are parallel within a response; the vertical offsets are baseline differences. 

trend_rows <- function(fit, response) {
  ov <- as.data.frame(confint(linear_heat(fit)))
  ov_p <- as.data.frame(summary(linear_heat(fit)))$p.value
  yr <- as.data.frame(confint(linear_heat(fit, by = "year")))
  yr_p <- as.data.frame(summary(linear_heat(fit, by = "year")))$p.value
  data.frame(Response = response,
             Period = c("Overall", paste0(yr$year)),
             Ratio = c(ov$ratio, yr$ratio),
             Lower = c(ov$lower.CL, yr$lower.CL),
             Upper = c(ov$upper.CL, yr$upper.CL),
             p = c(ov_p, yr_p))
}
trend_tab <- bind_rows(
  trend_rows(f_total,   "Total weight"),
  trend_rows(f_healthy, "Healthy weight")
) %>%
  mutate(`Per-pulse ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)",
                                               Ratio, Lower, Upper),
         p = fmt_p(p)) %>%
  select(Response, Period, `Per-pulse ratio (95% CI)`, p)

kable(trend_tab,
      caption = "Per-pulse linear trend among A–D (Control excluded), overall and by year. The model has no heat × cultivar interaction, so the trend is common to MQ and ST.")

Diagnostics are acceptable: dispersion, uniformity, and outlier tests are non-significant (the count model’s dispersion test is borderline, p ≈ 0.08). The pair random effect matters for the weights (ICC ≈ 0.19 total, 0.11 healthy); for the percentage models the pair variance is small and the treatment-specific dispersion captures most of the extra-binomial variation.

6.1 Sensitivity checks

gamma_total <- glmmTMB(total_weight ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                         year:cultivar + (1 | pair),
                       data = d, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
gamma_healthy <- glmmTMB(healthy_weight ~ heat_group * year + cultivar +
                           year:cultivar + (1 | pair),
                         data = d, family = Gamma(link = "log"))

  s <- as.data.frame(summary(emmeans(m, ~ heat_group, type = "response")))

}

Healthy-weight average heat/control ratio after dropping the most extreme plot: 0.816 (0.766, 0.868).

The Gamma model gives the same conclusions as the log-normal model, and dropping the most extreme healthy-weight plot changes the average heat/control ratio only slightly (0.804 → 0.816). The results are not driven by that one plot.

7. Summary for discussion

Final models.

Response Model Selected because
Total weight heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar + (1\|pair) heat profile differs by year; not by cultivar
Healthy weight same same
Healthy % by count heat_group + cultivar + year + (1\|pair), beta-binomial no heat interactions; additive
Healthy % by weight same, beta no heat interactions; additive

Key numbers.

Response Control Average of A–D Effect
Total weight 808 g 715 g −11.5%
Healthy weight 789 g 634 g −19.6%
Healthy % by count 95.4% 83.1% −12.3 pp (OR 0.24)
Healthy % by weight 97.9% 89.6% −8.3 pp (OR 0.19)

What changes when Control and A–D are at the same level.

  • The 5-level factor makes the heat profile explicit: each of A–D is compared with the same Control, and the model can test whether the shape of the profile differs by cultivar or year.
  • The shape does differ by year for the weights (heat_group × year p = 0.0003 total, p = 0.006 healthy). In 2024 the per-pulse trend is weak (about −3%, p ≈ 0.20); in 2025 it is strong (about −15%, p < 0.0001). A binary treatment × year term would miss this, because it only allows the overall OTC-vs-Control shift to differ by year, not the A–D shape.
  • The shape does not differ by cultivar for the weights (heat_group × cultivar p = 0.28/0.29), even though the binary treatment × cultivar test was borderline in the earlier parameterisation. The 4-df interaction has less power than the 1-df binary test, so the two parameterisations answer slightly different questions.
  • For the percentage outcomes, the profile is additive: no heat × cultivar, no heat × year, and the four heat levels are similar. The heat effect is a step change, not a dose–response.
  • Pooling controls is by design: all control plots are untreated. The separate-control check is not significant (H0 vs H4, 3 df: p = 0.79, 0.88, 0.12, 0.10), so the pooled-control model is used; the percentage checks are only moderately powered.

Points to discuss tomorrow.

  1. Heat × year for weights. Is the stronger 2025 dose–response real, or is it driven by a few plots (e.g. the 2025 MQ A/B and ST A/B plots with high rot)? The sensitivity check drops the most extreme healthy-weight plot and the average effect is stable, but the year-specific A–D shape deserves a closer look.
  2. Heat × cultivar. The 5-level test says no (p = 0.28/0.29); the binary treatment × cultivar test was borderline (p ≈ 0.05/0.046). Which parameterisation should we report? The 5-level model is the direct answer to “Control and A–D at the same level”; the binary model is more powerful for a single shift.
  3. Pooling controls. The controls are untreated, so they are pooled by design. The separate-control check is not significant (p = 0.10–0.88), but the percentage checks are only moderately powered. Is the design-based pooling sufficient, or should we report the separate-control model as a sensitivity?
  4. Percentage model. Additive 5-level model, no dose–response. Is the A–D difference (e.g. D worst for weight percentage, A worst for count) worth reporting, given that the per-pulse trend is not significant?
  5. Linear trend. The per-pulse contrast is computed only among A–D; Control is excluded. Is the equal-spacing assumption (1, 2, 3, 4 pulses) defensible, given that pulse timing also differs?
  6. Sample size. Three pairs per cell; the 4-df interactions are low-powered. Non-significant interactions should not be read as evidence of no effect.
